chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade 'al-kashuf', which is that the she-camel is bred while her offspring is still young, unless her offspring is given in charity or slaughtered. And he forbade a donkey from being mounted on an old female donkey.

key_terms.الْكَشُوف: A specific breeding practice where a she-camel is bred while her offspring is still young.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on breeding animals while their young are still dependent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic emphasis on animal welfare (rihla) by prohibiting 'al-kashuf', a practice of overbreeding where a she-camel is kept pregnant while nursing a young offspring, unless the calf is freed via charity or slaughter. The second prohibition against mounting a young donkey on an old one reflects the principle of avoiding undue burden or mismatched pairing, ensuring the well-being of both animals. These rulings underscore the Shia scholarly tradition's view that kindness to animals is an integral part of faith and practical jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from the exposure, and it is that the she-camel is connected (given away) for the breeding and her children are young, except if he gives in charity with her children, or is slaughtered, and he<sup>saww</sup> forbade from making a donkey leap upon an old one’.
en.sarwar: 24. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited exposing a she-camel before a he-camel for breeding, unless the young is given in charity or is slaughtered as well as a donkey to leap (mount) over an old one.’”
